content:
Your venue comparison identifies a promising place to meet. Before you commit, check the written terms for the rooms, activities and hours your church needs. Keep unresolved permissions separate from the venue's score.

Use this checklist with the proposed agreement, current fee schedule and insurance instructions in front of you. Bring unclear terms to a local attorney and insurance questions to your agent.

---

## Start with access and legal scope

Under the federal Americans with Disabilities Act, religious entities are exempt from Title III. Public entities are subject to Title II. The Department of Justice describes these as different obligations, so ask an attorney which rules apply to the parties and activities in your arrangement.

Review practical access alongside that legal discussion. Washington's Education Ombuds checklist asks about parking, entrances, routes to meeting rooms, restrooms and emergency exits. Use those questions to check the specific areas offered to you.

<Callout type="warning">
This is general guidance, not legal advice. The district agreements below are local examples. Ask a local attorney to review your proposed agreement before signing.
</Callout>

---

## Name the use, rooms and hours

Ask the venue to identify your permitted activities and each room included. Describe worship and children's activities rather than leaving the use unclear. Fairfax County Public Schools in Virginia uses an agreement specifically for religious and cultural programs. Its sample excludes storage, so ask about equipment storage separately.

Check access before and after the gathering. Fairfax's auditorium guidelines include setup and breakdown in requested time, tie fees to total time in the building, and require separate requests for dressing rooms.

- [ ] Which rooms are included, and which need separate approval?
- [ ] Do the requested hours include setup, sound checks and teardown?
- [ ] Are additional rehearsal dates included?
- [ ] What equipment must you request separately?

---

## Price the whole reservation

Use the owner's current quote to fill in the cost questions below. Clover Park School District in Washington separates space rental from special equipment and lighting. Its guidance also describes staffing charges, possible security and possible cleaning or damage deposits.

| Item | Question to resolve |
|---|---|
| Space | Which rooms and hours does the quote cover? |
| Staff | Which employees are required, and what time is billable? |
| Equipment | What is included, and what costs extra? |
| Deposits | What is refundable, and under what conditions? |
| Payment | When is payment due, and what confirms the booking? |

Clover Park describes its booking fee as nonrefundable and says the booking is not confirmed until payment of that fee. Ask your venue how its own process works. Keep the booking payment separate from questions about cleaning and damage deposits.

<Callout type="important">
Examples were checked October 15, 2026. Confirm current terms, fees, deadlines and insurance requirements with Fairfax County Public Schools, Frederick County Public Schools or Clover Park School District before relying on their examples. Confirm current federal accessibility guidance with the Department of Justice and Texas insurance guidance with the Texas Department of Insurance where relevant.
</Callout>

---

## Check insurance against the policy

Give your agent the venue's written insurance instructions. Clover Park asks for a certificate showing the district as both certificate holder and additional insured. Ask what your own venue requires and which policy documents support that status.

The Texas Department of Insurance explains that certificate wording cannot expand policy coverage. Its guidance also says a certificate's cancellation-notice provision cannot go beyond the policy's requirements. These are Texas examples of why the underlying documents matter.

<Callout type="tip">
Ask your agent to show the policy or endorsement supporting an additional-insured request. Texas insurance guidance permits requesting policy copies. Keep the coverage question separate from what appears in the certificate-holder box.
</Callout>

---

## Read what the signature commits you to

Look for personal payment obligations as well as obligations of the church. Fairfax's religious and cultural sample makes the signer financially liable if the organization does not pay in full. Ask your attorney what the signature would mean under your agreement.

Read indemnity and hold-harmless language with the attorney, too. Fairfax's sample places liabilities arising from the organization's use on the organization and includes attorneys' fees. Ask which losses you would accept and which your insurer would cover.

Do not treat a certificate of insurance as an answer to every contractual promise. Compare the agreement with the actual policy documents.

---

## Check cancellation in both directions

Ask what happens when you cancel, when the owner needs the space, and when weather closes the building. Fairfax's sample allows relocation or cancellation because of school activities and programs.

Frederick County Public Schools in Maryland says event cancellations and modifications must be made by email to its coordinator and school site administrators at least 10 calendar days before the event. It says full facility fees and/or custodian fees apply when cancellation or modification occurs less than 10 calendar days before the event.

Use that as a local example of a deadline to record accurately. Ask your venue about the notice method, recipients, charges and any refund terms. Distinguish cancellation of one gathering from ending the whole agreement.

---

## Check the end date and renewal

Read the start and end provisions before planning beyond the term. New York City's commercial-leasing guide recommends negotiating a renewal option and addressing how renewal rent will be determined. Use that as a discussion prompt for your arrangement, without assuming a recurring school permit works like a commercial lease.

Ask whether continued use needs a new application, written renewal or another approval. If there is a renewal option, ask how to exercise it and how the next price is set. Keep the owner's answer with the proposed terms.

---

## Review the final packet

Return to unresolved permissions and costs from your venue comparison. Consider an attorney's review of unclear lease terms, as the Small Business Administration suggests.

- [ ] Match the rooms, activities and access hours to your request.
- [ ] Match the quote to the staff and equipment you need.
- [ ] Review liability wording and insurance documents with the appropriate professionals.
- [ ] Record cancellation and renewal instructions before committing.

<Callout type="scripture">
*"Without consultation, plans are frustrated, But with many counselors they succeed."* — Proverbs 15:22 (LSB)
</Callout>

claim_check.notes: Author checked source claims and exact verse; independent Opus review of claims, scripture and full screenshots remains required. As of October 15, 2026. Checklist questions are applications of cited terms, not asserted legal requirements.

rulings: Resolved: cover federal ADA entity scope before local agreement examples; do not give a universal worship-use entitlement or accessibility exemption for the venue.
Resolved: present local agreement provisions as questions for the proposed rental. Omit local dollar limits and payment deadlines except the precisely sourced Frederick cancellation example.
Resolved: preserve A23 separation of permission and scoring, and the insurance article distinction between a certificate and policy coverage.
Resolved: quote Proverbs 15:22 exactly as a standalone scripture callout without a new theology or methodology claim.
